name: FL-24
label: Safe D

key_factors: Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~96%
Open seat with no incumbent advantage, but Democratic nominee heavily outspent
Large outside spending opposing the Democrat, a minor wrinkle
model.rationale: This Miami-area open seat carries a D+22 partisan lean and no expert rater flags it as competitive, while Polymarket prices the Democrat near 96%. The heavy outside spending against Gilbert is the only notable counter-signal, justifying a small trim from the fundamentals-based margin.
model.watch: A surge of outside spending against Gilbert or a weak Democratic primary nominee could narrow the margin, though a Republican win would require an unusually large shift.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Frederica Wilson (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Frederica Wilson's retirement leaves this heavily Democratic South Florida seat open, but the district's D+22 partisan lean makes it very difficult terrain for Republicans. Oliver Gilbert has raised over $800,000 and benefits from substantial outside support, though outside groups have also spent more than $2 million opposing him. Republican Te Mayonna Brown has modest resources and no outside backing.

No public general-election polls are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and prediction markets, which price the Democratic nominee around 96% to win. The race is rated Safe Democratic, with the main uncertainty being the size of the margin rather than the winner.
